title: Did you know… Joseph stayed faithful even when forgotten in prison?
paragraphs: Did you know… Joseph stayed faithful even when forgotten in prison?

He wasn’t just imprisoned.
He was forgotten.
By the very man he helped.

No applause.
No rescue.
No timeline update from God.
Just silence.
Joseph—the dreamer, the favored son—went from visions to chains. Sold by brothers. Falsely accused. Locked in a dungeon for doing what was right (see Genesis 39–40).
And then comes the line that stings:
“The chief cupbearer… did not remember Joseph, but forgot him.” (Genesis 40:23)
Forgotten.

After interpreting his dream.
After asking for just one thing: “Remember me.”
But heaven didn’t move.
But here’s what we miss…
God was still writing.

In the dark.
In the delay.
In the silence that felt like abandonment.

Joseph stayed faithful when no one was watching.
He kept serving when nothing was changing.
He honored God when it seemed like God had gone quiet.
That’s not weakness.
That’s worship.
And then—suddenly.

A door.
A call.
A crown.
From prison to palace in a single divine moment (Genesis 41).
Because God’s delay is never His denial.
Maybe that’s you right now.

You did right.
You stayed clean.
You served faithfully.
And still… you feel overlooked.
Forgotten.
Listen—

You are not buried.
You are being planted.
And when God lifts you, no man can take credit.
Jesus knows this place too.

Betrayed.
Abandoned.
Left to die.
But three days later—resurrection power rewrote the story.
That same grace is writing yours.
God hasn’t lost your name.
He’s preparing your moment.
From silence to sovereignty. From prison to purpose.
